minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 16, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:03 p.m., on June 16, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on June 11, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:08 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness (arrived at 5:05 p.m.)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

 CS1. Conference With Real Property Negotiators Pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.8. Property: That Portion of Oso Creek Trail System Owned by American
  Golf (The Open Space Located Between Casta Del Sol Road and Jeronimo Road -
  The Tennis Pavilion to the West and the Casta Del Sol Residential Community to the
  East.) City Negotiators: City Manager Dennis Wilberg and Assistant City Manager
  Keith Rattay. Owner’s Negotiators: American Golf President. Under Negotiation:
  Price and Terms.

City Council Minutes  1  June 16, 2014
  CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Reardon

INVOCATION: Mayor Kelley

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two matters in Closed
Session. The City Council gave direction to staff but no reportable action occurred. The Council
will adjourn into Closed Session at the end of the open session.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Featured Business of the Month - Rejoice Christian Bookstore

  Mayor Kelley presented proclamation to Kimberly Jackson.

P2. Recognize City Volunteers for Their 1,000 Hours of Service

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of appreciation to (1) Donna Serizawa and Jerry Toice
  for volunteer hours at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center; and (2)
  Lowell Simon for volunteer hours with the Senior Community Activity Team (SCAT).

P3. School Spotlight - Viejo Elementary

  The City Council received a presentation from Principal Doug Kramer.

P4. School Spotlight - Newhart Intermediate

  The City Council received a presentation Principal Jeff Jones.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Tiffany McCafferty, Health Educator, Rebecca Yee and Lela Salem, Community of Character
Youth Committee, M.V.: spoke about The National Council on Alcoholism & Drug

City Council Minutes  2  June 16, 2014
 Dependence-Orange County (NCADDOC) and thanked local vendors who participated in the
Responsible Beverage Service Training Program.

Lynn Pipitone, M.V.: voiced concerns regarding the Planning and Transportation
Commission's denial of her Architectural Review for the remodel of an existing single-story,
single-family residence located at 26671 Castile Lane. She asked that the City Council review
her case at a future meeting.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed the City of Laguna Hills Police Study Report regarding the
lowering of police costs without sacrificing service.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 9, 11, 14, 15, 19, 20, and 22 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate
discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of June 2, 2014, as presented.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April 2014

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for April 2014

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for April
  2014
City Council Minutes  3  June 16, 2014
   Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for April 2014

  Received and filed.

10. Agreement for Consultant Services for Property Tax and Financial Consulting (HdL
  Coren & Cone)

  Approved the agreement for Consultant Services with HdL Coren & Cone (A14-17) for
  property tax and financial consulting services for an amount not to exceed $16,500 for the
  one-year period of July 1, 2014 - June 30, 2015 with authority for extension and additional
  fees up to a cumulative amount of $33,000 as set forth in the Agreement.

12. Agreement for Oversight Board Legal Services (Harper & Burns LLP)

  Approved the agreement for Oversight Board Legal Services with Harper & Burns LLP
  (A14-19) in an amount not to exceed $5,000 for each six-month Recognized Obligation
  Payment Schedule (ROPS) period.

13. Agreement for Consultant Services (Arbitrage Compliance Specialists)

  Approved the agreement for Consultant Services (Arbitrage Compliance Specialists, Inc.)
  (A14-20) for Arbitrage Compliance services in an amount not to exceed $1,250 for services
  related to the Mission Viejo Community Development Finance Authority Variable Rate
  Demand Revenue Bonds (Mission Viejo Mall Improvement Project) 1999 Series A for the
  period of July 1, 2014 - June 30, 2015 as set forth in the Agreement.

16. Annual Weed Abatement Program for Parcels Under One Acre - Year 2014 Phase 1

  (1) Adopted Resolution 14-23 Declaring that Certain Weeds, Rubbish, Refuse, and Dirt on
  Parcels Under One Acre Constitute Nuisances; Declaring the Intention of the City Council
  to Order the Abatement of Said Nuisances; and Fixing a Time and Place for Hearing
  Protests; (2) instructed the Public Services Department to mail a Notice to Destroy Weeds
  in accordance with Section 39566 of the Government Code; and (3) instructed the City
  Clerk to set the Public Hearing for August 18, 2014.

17. Oso Parkway Widening, I-5 Freeway to Country Club Drive (CIP 791)

  Approved the agreement with HDR Construction Control Corporation (A14-23) in the
  amount of $185,562 for construction management services for the subject project.

18. 2013 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
City Council Minutes  4  June 16, 2014
   authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

21. Youth Services Program Contract Amendment

  Amended the Contract with the Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD)
  Department of Recreation and Community Services to provide youth services programs
  through Fiscal Year 2014-15 in the amount not to exceed $742,000.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

19. Muirlands Boulevard Street Lights (CIP 222)

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Lin Marelic, M.V.: spoke in favor of the project.

  The following provided written statements in favor of the project: Jack Goldstein, M.V.;
  Hollis Pass, M.V.; Lin Marelic, M.V.; and Branko Marelic, M.V.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she wants to reconsider the impact or the amount of
  lighting that is being requested and to consider solar lights. She expressed concern that the
  city has too much lighting and she suggested less impactful illumination.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
  bid specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

23. Adoption of the Revised FY 2014-15 City Operating and Capital Improvement
  Program Budget

  Mayor Kelley requested that Item #32 be moved up for consideration after the budget staff
  report.

City Council Minutes  5  June 16, 2014
   City Manager Dennis Wilber and Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas
  presented the staff report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

32. Shade Canopies for Tennis Center Benches

  Mayor Kelley presented the staff report.

  Wil Garcia, M.V.: spoke in favor of purchasing shade canopies for the Tennis Center
  benches.

  The following provided written statements in favor of the shade canopies: Linda Powell,
  M.V.; Sandra Fish, M.V.; Christine Douglas, M.V.; James Saltl, M.V.; Gloria Byrne, M.V.;
  Martha Casey, M.V.; and Robert Breton, M.V.

  Council Member Reardon asked for clarification regarding the size and type of canopies
  that will be installed. She also expressed concern about the lack of shade at the Felipe
  Tennis Center and asked that the Wheelchair Tennis Camp be held at the Marguerite
  Tennis Center. She further asked staff to provide an update on enrollment and fee rates.

  Council Member Schlicht noted that other facilities have not been enhanced and she stated
  that this is an uneven expenditure of tax dollars.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to include shade
  canopies for the tennis center benches in the mid-cycle budget update.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury
  NOES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Mayor Kelley thanked her fellow Council Members for their support and asked that the
  $40,000 be added into the budget discussions.

RECESS

At the hour of 8:25 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:32
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  6  June 16, 2014
 OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

23. Adoption of the Revised FY 2014-15 City Operating and Capital Improvement
  Program Budget

  Council Member Schlicht requested that the recommended action be bifurcated.

  Mayor Kelley noted that the $40,000 approval for the tennis benches and shade canopies
  will come out of the reserve balance of $186,738 that is in excess of the 50% Reserve level
  projected for June 30, 2015.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley to adopt
  Resolution 14-25* Adopting a Revised Budget for the City of Mission Viejo for FY 2014-
  15 and Appropriating Funds for FY 2014-15;

  *Council Members Reardon and Schlicht voted no on the tennis benches and shade
  canopies portion of this resolution only.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness to adopt
  Resolution 14-26, Amending the City's salary schedule and establishing salary ranges for
  authorized job classifications;

  Council Member Schlicht expressed that she would be voting no because Mission Viejo is
  pretty high right now as far as total wages per resident for the South County area.

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Schlicht suggested that next four recommended actions be addressed
  together.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon to (1) adopt
  Resolution 14-27 Modifying the Employer Paid Member Contributions for the
  miscellaneous group to the California Public Employees Retirement System, effective June
  7, 2014; (2) adopt Resolution 14-28, Modifying the Employer Paid Member Contributions
  for the miscellaneous group to the California Public Employees Retirement System,
  effective June 6, 2015; (3) adopt Resolution 14-29, Modifying the Employer Paid Member
  Contributions for the senior executive group to the California Public Employees Retirement
  System, effective June 7, 2014; and (4) adopt Resolution 14-30, Modifying the Employer
City Council Minutes  7  June 16, 2014
   Paid Member Contributions for the senior executive group to the California Public
  Employees Retirement System, effective June 6, 2015;

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley to approve the ninth
  amendment to the City Manager employment agreement;

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness to (8)
  approve the second amendment to the Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  employment agreement.

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (CONTINUED)

3.  Check Register Dated May 23, 2014 in the Amount of $1,927,601.85

4.  Check Register Dated May 30, 2014 in the Amount of $974,486.54

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the Jason Harnett consultation fees for
  the ITF World Championship Tournament. She also inquired about payments to Nichols
  Consulting and GSL consulting and asked that items 3 and 4 be taken together.

  City staff provided responses.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the
  accompanying check registers for items 3 and 4.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  8  June 16, 2014
 *Agenda item 11 was taken out of order.

11. Agreement for Consultant Services (KNN Public Finance)

  Council Member Schlicht asked staff to provide clarification in regards to the contract.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas provided a response.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  Agreement for Consultant Services (KNN Public Finance) (A14-18) for public finance
  advisory services for an amount not to exceed $25,000 for services related to the Mission
  Viejo Community Development Finance Authority Variable Rate Demand Revenue Bonds
  (Mission Viejo Mall Improvement Project) 1999 Series A for the period of July 1, 2014 -
  June 30, 2015 as set forth in the Agreement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

9.  Mission Viejo Community Facilities District No 92-1 - Annual Special Tax for Fiscal
  Year 2014-15

  Director Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  adopt Resolution 14-22 Establishing an Annual Special Tax for Fiscal Year 2014-15 for
  Community Facilities District No. 92-1 (Mission Viejo Freeway Center).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

14. Ordinance to Repeal City Ordinance No. 12-292 and Thereby Remove Chapter 11.23
  of Title 11 from the Mission Viejo Municipal Code

  Council Member Schlicht stated she would be voting no to be consistent with her prior vote
  on this ordinance.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to adopt Ordinance 14-
  303 Repealing Ordinance 12-292 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code.

City Council Minutes  9  June 16, 2014
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

15. Marguerite Parkway Median Island Improvements, Via Florecer to Trabuco Road
  (CIP 220)

  Council Member Schlicht stated she was voting no to be consistent with her prior vote.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  award a contract to Green Giant Landscape, Inc. (A14-21) for the Marguerite Parkway
  Median Island Improvements in an amount not to exceed $316,357.00; (2) award a contract
  to the Orange County Conservation Corps, (OCCC) (A14-22) in an amount not to exceed
  $18,582.00; and (3) adopt Resolution 14-24 Amending the Fiscal Year 2013-2014 Budget
  for Capital Improvement Project 220.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

20. Barranca Parkway/Muirlands Boulevard Traffic Signal Synchronization (Project P)-
  Cooperative Agreement (CIP 217)

  Council Member Schlicht expressed safety concerns while traveling south on Muirlands
  Boulevard. She stated that the traffic signals are not in view at both Muirlands and
  Marathon, and Muirlands and Robin Circle due to the height of the trees.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  Cooperative Agreement No. CIP 331402 between the City of Irvine, the City of Lake
  Forest, and the City of Mission Viejo (A14-24) for the Barranca Parkway/Muirlands
  Boulevard Traffic Signal Synchronization (Project P).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

22. Community Services Commission Vacancy

  Council Member Schlicht asked for clarification on the appointment process to fill this
  vacancy.
City Council Minutes  10  June 16, 2014
   Mayor Kelley noted that the resigning commissioner was appointed by Council Member
  Reardon so she will make a recommendation for a new member to fill the remainder of the
  two-year term.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to receive
  the letter of resignation from Community Services Commissioner Robert Breton.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness , Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

24. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

25. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

26. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

27. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

28. SCAG Transportation Committee (TC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg distributed a memo from Mark Nix, Director of Recreation and
Community Services, regarding the survey on the installation of a playground at Sierra

City Council Minutes  11  June 16, 2014
 Recreation Center. Mr. Wilberg announced that this project will be on the next City Council
Meeting Agenda.

29. Revisions to the City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she feels the Whistle Blower Policy had more
  protection for the employee than the previous policy. She also asked the City Attorney how
  the ethics hotline procedures would be handled and if there will be a dedicated phone line
  for this hotline.

  City Attorney Curley provided a response.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt
  Resolution 14-31, Providing for the Revisions to Personnel Policies.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (continued)

30. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon commended staff on the 20th Anniversary Relay for Life event. She
spoke about employee Rouhie Bosserman who has cancer and asked that Rouhie be remembered
in everyone’s prayers. Council Member Reardon read the speech by Sheila Boswell who was the
keynote speaker at the opening of the Relay for Life. She announced that on June 24, 2014, at
7:00 p.m. there will be a showing of “Behind the Orange Curtain” at St. Kilian Catholic Church
and she encouraged residents to attend. She gave statistics on “fatherless homes” and she
thanked the fathers sitting on the dais, in the audience and on city staff.

City Council Minutes  12  June 16, 2014
 Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht reiterated that the salary survey she handed out was to show
transparency to taxpayers. She said that benefits are still a burden that is being shouldered by the
taxpayers and that the problem is not going away regardless of who voted for the benefits plans.
She stated that her reason for the no vote on the Muirlands Lighting Project was because she
feels that solar lighting should have been considered. Council Member Schlicht commented on
the ITF Tennis Tournament, stating that she still is against public funds funding a private
organization and giving $9,000 to a tennis pro for consulting services. She stated that the
expenses for the tennis center were supposed to come from park fees but her recollection is that
it mostly came out of the general fund. She does not feel the additional cost for the shade
canopies is necessary at this time. Council Member Schlicht ended her comments with a quote
from Galileo: “All Truths are easy to understand once they are discovered; the point is to
discover them.”

Council Member Ury

Thanked Council Member Reardon for her kind words. He also thanked staff and his colleagues
for their patience during his run for the Board of Supervisors.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Announced that the DAWG walk is this Saturday, June 21, 2014, and he invited residents to
attend. He noted that the Rotary gave out scholarships this year and it was a great experience to
see the students so appreciative.

Mayor Kelley

31. Water Safety Presentations

  Mayor Kelley presented her report.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve water
  safety/drowning prevention presentations at Sierra Recreation Center on June 26 and the
  Marguerite Aquatics Center on July 10, 2014.

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness commented that it would be beneficial for parents to have a list
  of locations for swim lessons at the presentations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  13  June 16, 2014
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 10:13 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 10:52 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that there was no reportable action from Closed Session.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:53 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, July 7, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of July 7, 2014

City Council Minutes  14  June 16, 2014
